title: The Rite of the Last Candle
author: Flamekeeper's Book
pages: When a soul goes out, the hearth of the house is banked low, never put out. The body is washed with warm water and laid with its feet toward the fire, so it may walk home if it wishes.
Kin keep vigil a night and a day. A beeswax candle is lit from the house fire and carried before the body to the yard. If it gutters on the way, the dead have something left to say.
Lay them in the earth with a coal from their own hearth at their breast. Raise the mound. Set the stone. Place the candle on the stone and say their name three times, loud enough for the street.
Each year, on the death-day and at the Lantern Vigil, relight the candle. A grave that stays dark a full year is unremembered, and the unremembered grow cold, and the cold wander.
If you must move away, ask a neighbour to keep your candles, and pay them in kind. The Flamekeeper will witness it in the roll. No one should be forgotten for want of a penny's wax.
